post.title: Innernet
post.hook: What if your Programming folder had its own Google and its own Wikipedia?
post.summary: Innernet crawls the folders on your machine into a local search engine and an encyclopedia called Innerpedia, with agent dot folders indexed beside projects. It shipped a public demo and a narrated field guide film in two days of commits.
post.writeup:
## What it is

Innernet is a personal internet made from your folders. A crawler reads READMEs, manifests and Git metadata, builds a local JSON index, and two readers sit on top: a search engine with operators, and Innerpedia, an article for every project.

## Why

Projects pile up across a machine and are hard to rediscover. Innernet borrows the web's best habits (one search box, blue links, the encyclopedia) so your own work reads like a small connected web. Everything stays local: the server binds to 127.0.0.1 and secret folders such as `.ssh` or `.aws` are never entered.

## How it works

The crawl writes `data/index.json`; pages render from it, and search runs on the server with MiniSearch. Dot folders such as `.claude`, `.codex` and `.xo` become agent articles, with instructions, memory and session counts but never session contents. Page visits are kept as plain history files, with a copy in PGlite and an optional remote database. A public demo on Vercel indexes the open source quirq-ai repositories instead.

The stack is Next.js, React, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS. Sources can also include up to 50 public GitHub repositories, listed one at a time.

## Results

The repo holds 373 files and 16 commits, all from 2026-10-02 to 2026-10-03. A 2:49 explainer film, narrated and built in HyperFrames as engraved plates, plays at the top of the in-app field guide. The index stays near 70 MB for 5,000 pages, however often it is rebuilt.

## Open questions

The README's own docs and the storyboard disagree on film length (2:21.5 planned, 169s in the final plan), so the cut deserves a final check. The demo's 30 day anonymous history also invites a look at how well it scales.
